entries.source_notes:
Reissue of [r=374507], originally released in 1965.  This variant is the first pressing of many under the GR-155 catalog number.  Issued in 1995, it has been out of print for many years.  It is distinguished by the following: 
--MASTERED BY CAPITOL machine stamped in deadwax. Very heavy vinyl (over 200 grams). 
--Orange, oval sticker on shrink which says "The Impulse! Reissue Series: Remastered original analog recording on limited edition heavy virgin vinyl; Original gatefold design; Custom packaging; Rare photos from original negatives; Original liner notes." 
--No black and gold sticker.

If you have GEO ⓤ in the runout, you have:
[r3313670] with Back to Black sticker or 
[r4773442]

If you have TML stamped in the runouts and a UPC that is oriented horizontally and has borders on all four sides you have [r7510344].

If you have none of these you might have [r5364985].

Jowcol Music [BMI]
Originally recorded December 9th, 1964.
Remastered at MCA Music Studios

℗ 1995 MCA Records, Inc & © 1995 GRP Records, Inc & © 1964 MCA Records, Inc
Made in USA
Distributed in the USA by Uni Distribution Corporation

Original introduction written by John Coltrane, a brief essay written in 1995 by Michael Cuscuna, and the poem "A Love Supreme" by Coltrane printed therein.

Label info:
Made in West Germany.
℗ 1965 Polydor International GmbH., Hamburg.

Box (general info):
The box is standard plain-textured with a picture fronted.
Box info (front):
Archiv Produktion / Johann Sebastian Bach / Weinachtsoratorium BWV 248 / Gundula Janowitz • Christa Ludwig • Fritz Wunderlich • Franz Crass / Münchener Bach-Chor • Münchener Bach-Orchester / Karl Richter 
Box info (back):
3 LP • Stereo 2722 024
Printed in West Germany by Schwerdtle & Schantz, Berlin.
Box info (spine):
Bach • Weihnachtsoratorium • Richter

Comes with a 8 page booklet with liner notes, lyrics, tracklist and credits in german. On page 2 is a painting of Johann Sebastian Bach.
Booklet info (page 7):
Quelle/Source: Autograph der Partitur , Staatsbibliothek Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Berlin (Mus. ms. Bach P 32).
Ausgaben/Editions:Faksimile-Ausgabe des Autographs  (vgl. Quelle), hrsg. von Alfred Dürr (Bärenreiter-Verlag, Kassel etc., 1960).
Bach-Gesamtausgabe, Bd. V/2, hrsg. von Wilhelm Rust (Breitkopf &Härtel, Leipzig, 1856).
Neue Ausgabe sämtlicher Werke, Serie II, Bd. 6, hrsg. von Walter Blankenburg und Alfred Dürr (Bärenreiter-Verlag, Kassel etc., 1960).
Aufnahme/Recording/Enregistrement:
München, Herkules-Saal der Residenz.
6.-15.2.1965 / 25.2.-4.3.1965 / 8.-9.,14.-15.6.1965. 
℗ 1965 Polydor International GmbH.

Page 6:
Bach-Bild: Gemälde, 1746 (Leipzig, Stadtgeschichtliches Museum).

Page 8:
Printed in Germany by Neef, Wittingen.

entries.source_notes:
Burlesque in Four Scenes (complete recording).

Cover Photo: Nijinsky as Petrouchka, Courtesy Roger Pryor Dodge Collection, Dance Section, New York Public Library

Long Playing 
Living Presence - High Fidelity
Margin Control

[Liner]
"Together with Stravinsky's  'Le Sacre du Printemps' (Mercury MG50030), Ravel's 'Daphnis and Chloë' (Mercury MG50046) and the Tchaikovsky dance masterpieces 'Swan Lake' (Mercury OL 3-102), 'Sleeping Beauty' (Mercury OL 3-103) and 'The Nutcracker' (Mercury OL 2-101), this disc of Stravinsky's Petrouchka takes its place among the series of definitive recorded documentations of ballet masterpieces undertaken by Antal Dorati and the Minneapolis Symphony Orchestra for Mercury Living Presence.

Recorded during March of 1955 in the Northrop Memorial Auditorium on the University of Minnesota campus, this performance was taken with a single Telefunken microphone and with the orchestra seated in normal concert arrangement on the stage. A special study was made of the auditorium reverberation characteristic and its relationship to the illusion of presence in solo and ensemble texture before arriving at a decision regarding the final microphone placement and the stage area where the orchestra would be seated. In short, special pains were taken to achieve a maximum of tonal "warmth" with no loss in clarity of orchestral texture. We call attention also to the balance of the important solo piano part in the Russian Dance and Petrouchka's Room episodes midway in Side 1, as well as to the percussion and brass through the whole of In the Moor's Room (latter third of Side 1) and to the muted trumpets which signalize the return of Petrouchka's ghost at the conclusion of the ballet (end of Side 2)."

entries.source_notes:
Contains inner record sleeve on plain thick paper, Angel  Records logo printed on top. 
Booklet made in printed in England. Outer cardboard sleeve and record, made in the USA. 

(From the booklet) Recording details:
Suite No.5. Recorded in Paris on 13 June , 1939, by Pablos Casals on master numbers 2LA 3126 to 3127 and 3130 to 3134 inclusive.
First issued in July , 1948, on record numbers DB 6541 to DBS 6544.
Transferred to LP in Paris in 1957 on master number 2XLA 334. 

Suite No.6. Recorded in Paris on 3 June, 1938, by Pablo Casals on master numbers 2LA 2593 to 2600 inclusive. 
First issued in December, 1938, on record numbers DB 3674 to 3677. 
Transferred to LP in Paris in 1957 on master number 2XLA 335.

Both Suites first issued on LP in July, 1957, on record number COLH18 in the "Gravures Illustres" series in France. Issued in England in December, 1957 in the "Great Recordings of the Century" series.
